subject: general
question: Lad Khan Temple is located in which of the following state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lad Khan Temple** is located in **Aihole**, which is situated in the **Bagalkot district** of the state of **Karnataka**, India.
 
• Constructed in the **5th century AD**, it is considered one of the oldest structures in the region and was built during the reign of the **Early Chalukya dynasty**.
 
• The temple is primarily dedicated to **Lord Shiva** and houses a **Shiva Linga** in its inner sanctum, although historical evidence suggests it might have been originally dedicated to **Surya** (the Sun God).
 
• The unusual name "**Lad Khan**" is not reflective of its religious origin; it is named after a **Muslim prince** who lived in the temple for a period during the **19th century**.
 
• The temple architecture is noted for its **square plan** and a **flat roof** made of massive **stone slabs**, representing a crucial phase in the evolution of **Hindu temple architecture** from cave shelters to free-standing structures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aihole: The Cradle of Indian Architecture:**

 
 
• **Aihole** is often described as the "**Cradle of Indian Temple Architecture**" because it served as a site where **Chalukyan architects** experimented with various styles and designs.
 
• The **Aihole complex** contains over **120 stone temples** dating from the **4th to the 12th century**, including the famous **Durga Temple** and the **Ravana Phadi Cave**.
 
 
 
• **Chalukyan Dynasty and Art:**
 
 
• The **Chalukyas of Badami** were great patrons of art and architecture, establishing their power in the **Deccan** region during the **6th century**.
 
• The architectural style developed by them is known as the **Vesara style**, which blends elements of the **Nagara** (North Indian) and **Dravida** (South Indian) styles of temple building.
 
• Their major centers of construction included **Badami**, **Aihole**, and **Pattadakal**.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Features of Lad Khan Temple:**
 
 
• The temple features a **Mukhamandapa** (pillared porch) and a **Sabhamandapa** (great hall) leading to the **Garbhagriha** (sanctum).
 
• The **pillars** are decorated with intricate carvings, and the exterior walls feature **lattice windows** (Jalis) that allow light to enter the interior, a characteristic feature of **early Chalukyan** work.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Geographical and Historical Context:**

 
 
• The temples at **Aihole**, **Badami**, and **Pattadakal** are located along the **Malaprabha River** valley in **Karnataka**.
 
• While **Aihole** was the early administrative center, **Pattadakal** eventually became the site for **royal coronations** and is now a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
 
 
• **Material and Construction:**
 
 
• The **Lad Khan Temple** was constructed using **sandstone** that was joined without mortar, using the **dry masonry** technique typical of the era.
 
• The **Nandi** (the sacred bull) is placed in the center of the hall, facing the **Shiva Linga**, which is a standard iconographic arrangement in **Shaivite temples**.
 
• The temple represents the **Panchayatana** style of architecture, though it is one of the more primitive versions of this layout.
